name: The Velvet Underground
hook: A New York band that sold few records in the 1960s and turned up, years later, behind Bowie, punk and post-punk.
blurb: The Velvet Underground formed in New York in 1965 around Lou Reed and John Cale, with Sterling Morrison and Maureen Tucker. Andy Warhol managed them and is credited as producer, alongside Tom Wilson, of their first album, 'The Velvet Underground & Nico' (Verve, 1967). They sang about drugs and city life when almost no one else did, and played loud, droning, repetitive rock. The record did not sell well at first, but musicians heard it: David Bowie was playing one of its songs before it was even released. Their reputation as the band nobody bought and everybody copied rests mostly on something Brian Eno said in 1982: that the first album sold about 30,000 copies in five years and every buyer started a band. The number is disputed. Wikipedia's article on the album cites MGM royalty statements showing 58,476 copies sold by February 1969. The influence is real and documented on this map through Bowie and Joy Division; the sales figure in the legend is not. Cale went on to produce the Stooges' first album. Reed left in 1970, and the band carried on under Doug Yule until 1973.

signatureTracks.title: I'm Waiting for the Man
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The song Bowie learned from an acetate before the album came out.

signatureTracks.title: Sister Ray
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Seventeen minutes of one riff and feedback, recorded live in the studio. Joy Division covered it on stage in 1980.
